name: Miguelina
band_note: ruled 14 Oct: resort house with no sweater; tops from $215 and dresses from $495, not the $423 blouse alone (thread proposal)
why: Women's cotton lace and embroidered resort dresses, caftans, tops and swim, mostly $350–$650, sold through its own site and a West Village store.

quote.q: What began as a personal solution quickly became the first women’s luxury apparel brand dedicated to travel.

opview: “What began as a personal solution quickly became the first women’s luxury apparel brand dedicated to travel.” — Miguelina (house), About, miguelina.com

craft_evidence.owned: no — own West Village store; no workroom named
craft_evidence.makers: partly — product pages credit 'handmade filé lace' made in Brazil and women's cooperatives by region (Tuscany, Papua New Guinea, Zambia, Brazil) on the Global page; makers not named individually. The
craft_evidence.mills: yes, on a capsule — 'woven in Tuscany by Busatti' (Miguelina x Busatti styles)
craft_evidence.madein: ~56% (32 of 57 styles: Made in the USA / New York, made in Brazil, woven in Tuscany)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated — label launched 1998 by Dominican-born designer Miguelina Gambaccini; not placed
craft_evidence.process: partial — handmade filé lace and cooperative weaving described; no making process for the main range
craft_evidence.reasoning: A named mill appears on the Busatti capsule ('woven in Tuscany by Busatti'), handmade filé lace from Brazil and named cooperative regions are credited, and over half the product pages state where the piece is made. Nothing is owned, and the main range names no maker. Names its mills on part of the range and owns nothing is a 3.
